EGF mRNA and peptide are upregulated in regenerative cirrhtic liver.
epidermal growth factors (EGFs) are over-expressed in regenerative hepatic tissue of cirrhotics.

the role of EGF in the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of cirrhosis.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of liver cirrhosis, a disease which affects 5% of the US population.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of growth factors and their receptors in cirrhotic disease.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EGF and its receptor (EGFR), which are normally expressed in the liver, are upregulated in cirrhotic disease.
we have shown that EGF and EGFR are expressed in regenerating cirrhotic livers and that EGF is upregulated.

the EGF/EGFR system is a major player in the development of cirrhosis.
